subject: SLA saturation lab plan & benchmark deliverables for Sigma-Ware RFP
messages:
From: Scott Molina <scott.molina@sigma-ware.com>

Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@sigma-ware.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: SLA saturation lab — data required for RFP

Hi Stephanie / Rishi,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we pull together the RFP appendix for the performance section, the procurement and infra teams at Sigma-Ware have asked for a concrete lab plan we can include as an attachment. Specifically they want: 

- Test methodology (how you generate traffic, warmup/run windows)
- Exact metrics collected (p50/p90/p99 latency, tail percentiles, tokens/sec, GPU util, mem pressure)
- Reproducibility checklist (seeds, model builds, quantization settings)
- Expected scaling curve (throughput vs. number of vhosts/GPUs) and a short table of observed numbers for a representative model (e.g., Llama-2-13B / 8k context)

Can you provide a brief lab plan + a template CSV we can drop into the RFP? We're on a tight timeline — the doc set is due to procurement by 10/28.

Also: we need to confirm the test harness you recommend for generating production-like request patterns (burstiness, short vs. long prompts). If you can call out recommended batch sizes and cache warmup strategy for our expected 100–400 qps steady state, that would be helpful.

Attaching a rough internal outline we've started.

Thanks,
Scott
Director, Cloud Ops — Sigma-Ware
[attachment: sigma-load-plan-draft.docx (docx)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA saturation lab — data required for RFP

Hi Scott / Priya,

Appreciate the clear ask — we've put together a focused lab plan and a downloadable benchmark template that matches the sections you outlined. Attached: 

- sigma-load-plan.xlsx (detailed run matrix)
- redwood-bench-template.csv (metrics table)
- redwood-arch-diagram.png (test topology reference)

High-level approach we recommend (summary):
1) Workload characterization: ingest a representative sample of your prompts (we recommend 5k–10k) split by short/medium/long; build a percentiles profile.
2) Deterministic runs: for each point on the run matrix (sequence length X QPS X batch size) perform 3 repeated runs with identical seeds and record p50/p90/p99, tokens/sec, and GPU-level telemetry.
3) Warmup & steady state: 10 minute warmup, 20 minute steady-state run. Verify KV-cache hit rates after warmup.
4) Saturation curve: increase offered load stepwise until either latency SLO breach or GPU saturation (>=92% sustained utilization) — capture per-step metrics.
5) Regression & reproducibility: archive model wheel, quantization artifacts, and a run manifest; supply a script and Docker image to re-run the same matrix.

Key recommended settings (initial):
- Reference model: Llama-2-13B (int8 quant) with 4k context for cost-forward runs; 8k for tail tests.
- Hardware: NVIDIA A10G / A100s (we'll provide exact kernel picks in the lab plan).
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8 — emphasize small-batch latency SLOs for interactive paths.
- Load generator: we recommend our in-house runner (open to using k6 for synthetic HTTP-level testing). It supports KV-cache priming and per-request token distributions.

I'll let Rishi and Dylan add the kernel/runtime and instrumentation details. We can do a quick screen-share on Friday to walk the plan and pin the matrix to Sigma-Ware's schedule.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: sigma-load-plan.xlsx (xlsx)]

Scott / team,

Adding the technical specifics for the RFP appendix and the bench template columns. Please see embedded checklist below — this is what we'll capture per-run and what you'll see in the CSV.

Run manifest & reproducibility:
- model_name, model_version, quantization (bits / method), wheel_sha256, tokenizer_version, random_seed
- runtime_kernel_version, cudnn/cu* combination, torch-trt or Triton variant if used

Telemetry and CSV columns (per-sample aggregated):
- run_id, timestamp_utc, offered_qps, achieved_qps, avg_tokens_per_request, p50_ms, p90_ms, p99_ms, p999_ms, tail_99_9_ms, tokens_per_sec, requests_per_second, gpu_util_pct, gpu_mem_used_mb, cpu_util_pct, rss_mb, kv_cache_hit_rate_pct, error_rate_pct, dropped_requests

Methodology notes:
- Warmup: 10 minutes with increasing QPS ramp (30s steps), then hold for steady-state window.
- Repeats: 3 sequential steady-state runs per matrix point; report median of medians, highlight variance.
- Load shapes: poisson arrival for interactive path; bursty Pareto/OnOff for background batch scoring.
- Tail-latency capture: enable high-resolution timers; export p99.9 and histograms.

Scaling behavior guidance you can include in the RFP:
- Horizontal scale: near-linear throughput increase up to GPU mem limits for small batch sizes; for large batches efficiency improves but latency increases nonlinearly.
- KV-cache: effective for repeated prefixes — priming reduces per-token compute; explicitly report cold vs warm-run numbers.

Instrumentation we will provide: Prometheus + Grafana dashboards (pre-built), a JSON run-manifest, and a Docker image with the exact runner.

I'll also prepare a short appendix blurb on interpreting the saturation curve (how to read inflection points and identify memory vs compute-bound regimes).

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
